name: Karin Karlsbro - Proposition de la Commission
title: Establishing the Ukraine Loan Cooperation Mechanism and providing exceptional macro-financial assistance to Ukraine
part_text:
The European Parliament backs a plan to lend Ukraine up to €45 billion, with €35 billion coming from the EU. Ukraine would not repay the loans directly. Instead, the money would come from windfall profits earned on Russian state assets frozen in the EU. The loans would run for 45 years and come with conditions on democracy, the rule of law and human rights. Parliament wants the plan adopted quickly so the money can be paid out by the end of 2024.

- **What changes:** The EU lends Ukraine up to €35 billion, repaid from profits on frozen Russian assets, not by Ukraine.
- **Who it affects:** Ukraine, EU taxpayers and the EU budget, which carries the risk if the assets are unfrozen.
- **What happens next:** Parliament approved the proposal without changes; EU governments must now agree so the loan can be paid out by the end of 2024.
